Heretic

HAIR-uh-tik -- stress on the first syllable, HAIR. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Heretic is a person who goes against established beliefs or doctrine.

In 1633, the astronomer was tried as a heretic for defending the idea that the Earth moves around the Sun.

Worked Example

In the history reading, a sixteenth-century printer is hauled before a tribunal for publishing pamphlets that contradict the church's official teachings.

Because he holds and spreads beliefs that go against the established doctrine, the authorities brand him a heretic. The word names a person -- usually one who believes deeply, just not what the officials say he must.

How Heretic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

dissenter

dissenter: one who disagrees with an official or majority position

nonconformist

nonconformist: one who refuses to follow accepted customs or beliefs

apostate

apostate: one who abandons or renounces a faith or cause

Antonyms

believer

believer: one who accepts and holds a faith or doctrine

conformist

conformist: one who follows established beliefs and customs

How Strong Is It? — dissenter → heretic → apostate

dissenter vs. heretic

dissenter vs. heretic: Dissenter is milder and broader than heretic -- a dissenter disagrees with an official position on some point, while a heretic is formally condemned for beliefs that strike at the established doctrine itself.

apostate vs. heretic

apostate vs. heretic: Apostate goes a step beyond heretic in the eyes of the authorities: a heretic believes the 'wrong' version of the faith, while an apostate has abandoned the faith altogether and walked away from it.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of heretic.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — heret

Root — heret: choosing, chosen (from Greek hairetikos, from hairein 'to choose')

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Heret ('choosing', from Greek hairein, 'to choose') + -ic spell heretic: literally 'one who chooses' -- someone who picks out their own belief instead of accepting the doctrine handed down by the authorities. To the officials, that act of choosing was the crime.

Use the root in a new word: heresy

Use the root in a new word: heresy: The tribunal condemned the philosopher's writings as heresy and ordered every copy burned.

Root Check

Word Choice

Heretic is a noun for a person: someone is 'branded a heretic' or 'tried as a heretic.' The matching adjective is 'heretical' -- heretical ideas, never 'heretic ideas.' Keep it distinct from atheist (a person who believes in no higher power at all): a heretic usually believes deeply, just differently from the official doctrine.
